clue.text: Rattle on, like the film star holding a book

indicators.note: the star's name has the book's letter held within it, like hands clasping something

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Someone chatters away like a Hollywood idol clutching a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To gabble is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly, which is what rattling on describes.

clue.text: Bridge built with a set method

parts.note: a gang is a set or group of people
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A bridge constructed using a fixed technique.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is a movable walkway bridging a ship and the quay, so a bridge.

clue.text: Brother has personal camel

parts.note: own means belonging to oneself, personal

explanation.surface: A man's sibling owns his very own camel.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel is a light yellowish-brown colour, so it is a shade of the colour named.

clue.text: Head lad might speak thus

indicators.note: these letters might be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior stable hand talks in this affected way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: the letters of 'Head lad' rearranged give the posh phrase such a lad might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in an affected, pretentiously refined manner is called talking all posh and genteel this way.

clue.text: A rise, like a hundredth of a dollar

parts.note: as can mean like, in the sense of similar to
a cent is one hundredth of a US dollar

explanation.surface: A tiny price increase, compared to a single cent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is an upward climb or rise, so the two noun phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: She does not want you to see any more of her

definitions.text: She does not want you to see any more of her

parts.words: She does not want you to see any more of her
parts.note: reads like a jilted lover, but describes a dieter keen for there to be less of her body to see

explanation.surface: A woman breaking off a relationship, wanting nothing more to do with you.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieter wants to shed weight so that there is less of her for anyone to see.

clue.text: Fancy brewing a beer? A lot!

indicators.note: brewing stirs and ferments ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone is brewing a lot of beer at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate or ornate, which is what fancy means as an adjective.

clue.text: The more curious formula

indicators.note: curious means strange, suggesting the letters are in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: The more you look at a formula, the stranger it gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proven mathematical statement, often expressed as a formula.

clue.text: Long snake that is squeezing a queen

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the that-is abbreviation squeezes the queen's letter between its own

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R stands for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A long snake crushing a queen, as Cleopatra's asp did.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to long for or yearn after something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: His teacups I don't break, so I'm innocent

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order, just as a careless guest breaks crockery

explanation.surface: A guest promises not to break the host's cups, protesting innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' signals rearranging HISTEACUPSIDONT; 'so I'm' simply leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsophisticated is naive and artless, which is the innocent sense of the word.

clue.text: One of a pair gets only half a stab of pain

parts.note: a twin is one of a pair born together

indicators.note: only the front half of the word gets is taken, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A twin feels a sharp pang, but only half as strong as the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden brief stab of pain, so the noun phrases match.

clue.text: Apology from Williams or Ryan

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the run of letters across these names

explanation.surface: An apology is issued by one of two people, Williams or Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you regret something in three words is the classic spoken apology.

clue.text: Look at a ghost as a protective shield

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a shade is a ghost or spirit, especially in classical poetry

explanation.surface: Gazing at a spectre while using something as a protective screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a visor worn to protect the eyes from glare, a kind of shield.

clue.text: Taxing is frustrating

definitions.meaning: taxing means demanding and causing strain
frustrating means exasperating and causing tension

explanation.surface: Paying tax is so annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both taxing and frustrating situations cause strain and anxiety, the core sense here.

clue.text: Genuine woman's address in the provinces

parts.note: real means genuine
Ms is a form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A real lady's home address is out in the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or domains, so the word works as a synonym for provinces or territories.

clue.text: Excluded from pub, getting angry

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking room
red is the colour of anger, as in seeing red

explanation.surface: A drinker thrown out of the pub gets furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be barred is to be banned or excluded from a place, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Execute stunted boss in avenue

indicators.note: the shortened boss sits in the avenue abbreviation
stunted means cut short, so the boss word loses its final letter

parts.note: a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: Killing a short boss in the street, gangland style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' tempts toward killing, but here it means carry out; 'stunted' trims the boss by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan is to carry it out, which is to achieve it.

clue.text: Tutor has solutions for foolish people

parts.note: a don is a university tutor
keys are the solutions or answers to puzzles

explanation.surface: A tutor holds the answers that foolish students need.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys is a colloquial term for stupid people, after the animal's dull reputation.

clue.text: Game to hire during the journey

indicators.note: the hiring word comes during, so inside, the journey word

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey
to let is to hire out, as with a flat

explanation.surface: A game played while renting something on the way somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Go off, having scoffed roll

parts.note: to rot is to go off, as food does
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A bread roll eaten after it has gone stale.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn or roll around an axis, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Weak conciliators must get a report

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, acts as a conciliator between countries
a report is a loud sound, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: Feeble peacemakers must produce an official report.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsound is weak or unstable, as in an unsound structure.

clue.text: A small amount stuck on a rod for a larva

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
a pole is a long rod

explanation.surface: A dab of bait fixed to a fishing rod for a grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larva of a frog or toad, a specific example.

clue.text: Horse-box needs a fan

parts.note: a chest is a large box
a nut is an enthusiast or fan, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A horse trailer needs a ventilation fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse-box' reads as one vehicle, but the hyphen splits the definition from the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour, a common way to name a horse.

clue.text: Cheap and nasty cast broken by deviant

indicators.note: the throwing word is split open with the strange word inserted

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy
odd means deviant or abnormal

explanation.surface: A cheap production whose cast is spoilt by a wayward actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made and of poor quality, which is cheap and nasty.

clue.text: Ring true falsely, which is weird

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring

indicators.note: falsely suggests the word true is made untrue by rearranging it

explanation.surface: A bell rings false, which is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre means unconventional or bizarre, borrowed from French, so it matches weird.

clue.text: Lost cur infested with disorder is what Hamlet discussed

indicators.note: letters in disorder are jumbled, so these words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stray dog crawling with parasites is the subject of Hamlet's musings.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's 'To be or not to be' soliloquy weighs whether to take his own life.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's famous speech debates suicide, killing oneself, which this compound names.

clue.text: Volunteer is oddly silent

indicators.note: the word silent is arranged in an odd, unusual way

explanation.surface: A volunteer who is strangely quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for service voluntarily, the verb sense of volunteer.

clue.text: Nowadays present in cement

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of years
here means present, as when answering a register

explanation.surface: Modern gifts find themselves set in concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, as two surfaces joined by cement are made to bond.
